answer: An agent booking saffron shipments from a mesa farm to a jetty should earn reputation only from deliveries confirmed by independently sampled receivers. Give each physical shipment one receipt and one reputation budget; splitting its seller into aliases only divides that budget. A farmer seeking extra influence must arrange additional real deliveries and pay transport costs. Receivers can still collude or sell confirmations, while shared logistics can link honest firms, so audit random parcels and allow evidence-based disputes. A receipt proves a delivery claim, not a unique owner.
